argument_summary: The admissible record supports a narrow certification position, not a clean no-limitations certification. Aggregate readiness passed by 2.1 percentage points and launch rehearsal had no severity-one incidents, which supports launch readiness. At the same time, the HR benefits enrollment slice remains below target in a named launch use case, concentrated in leave-policy eligibility guidance, and the current mitigation artifact is still a draft with owner and threshold marked TBD. The supportable packet therefore defends certification only if it is framed as qualified and paired with explicit disclosure of that limitation in the model materials.
claims_about_business_cost: No business-cost claim is needed to justify the position. The supportable argument rests on the admissible readiness evidence plus disclosure and monitoring requirements, not on launch-pressure considerations.
claims_about_policy: The policy does not support treating the draft runbook as removing the disclosure obligation. The admissible policy text says certification without material caveats requires either current evidence that no material weakness remains or an approved mitigation with owner, threshold, review date, and rollback criterion. The current evidence does not show either of those predicates. But the same policy also indicates that a current named-use-case weakness can be handled through disclosure unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch. Public model-card guidance and AI risk guidance reinforce disclosure and monitoring as appropriate supporting controls; they do not override the release policy, but they do support a caveated certification posture rather than escalation if the packet is narrowed to that claim.
concessions: The evidence does not support a clean certification without material caveats.
The HR benefits enrollment weakness remains unresolved for a named launch use case.
The current mitigation runbook is draft-only and does not satisfy the policy standard for approved mitigation.
The current model-card draft text saying there are no known material limitations is not aligned with the admissible record.
